finding.claim: POP3 and IMAP retrievers disable TLS certificate verification when enable_ssl is set, so credentials and fetched mail are exposed to on-path MITM.
finding.source: Network attacker able to answer the TLS handshake for the configured IMAP/POP3 host (on-path or DNS/route hijack).
finding.sink: TLS session carrying user_name/password login and retrieved message bodies (pop3.rb:133, imap.rb:175).

trace.note: enable_ssl defaults to false; user sets it true via Mail.defaults retriever_method
enable_ssl(OpenSSL::SSL::VERIFY_NONE) hard-coded; no setting overrides it
pop3.start sends credentials over the unverified TLS session
Net::IMAP.new(..., settings[:enable_ssl], nil, false): fifth positional arg is verify, passed false
imap.login sends credentials over the unverified session

finding.guards_checked: No configuration key (pop3 defaults at pop3.rb:42-45, imap defaults at imap.rb:46-49) can change verify mode. SMTP is not affected: smtp.rb:96 exposes :openssl_verify_mode and smtp.rb:193-194 only overrides the default context when set, so peer verification stays on. IMAP positional semantics rely on Ruby stdlib net-imap signature, not verified in-repo.
